violations: The response prematurely inspected an empty workspace and requested repository materials that were unnecessary for defining the rule.
It settled on changing membership, revoking training access, and removing reminders without first resolving which meaning of inactive was intended.
arm_a.rationale: A added an unnecessary repository interruption and committed the recurring rule to both controls. The follow-up explicitly rejected its membership and training-access effects, so the initial delivery misses the resolved direction and requires nearly complete replacement.

violations: The failed workspace command was unnecessary because the requested policy clarification did not require repository inspection.
arm_b.rationale: B exposed the exact membership-versus-reminder decision with one bounded comparison and did not commit to an unstated effect. After clarification, it supplied a short if/then rule preserving membership and training access while removing reminders only.

violations: It assumed project permissions should remain without first resolving whether club departure also ended project participation.
It called the removal target a current-member permission list rather than the current-member roster named by the user.
arm_a.rationale: A guessed the permission consequence, but that guess matched the later clarification: project permissions remain. Its main defect is misnaming the roster as a permission list, which requires a small correction but leaves the two intended effects largely intact.

violations: It assumed departure should revoke permissions granted through club membership without clarifying how those permissions relate to project access.
Its permission-revocation rule conflicts with the instruction to retain project permissions until a project owner removes them.
arm_b.rationale: B correctly removes the person from the roster, but it invents a permission taxonomy and revokes a category of permissions immediately. The follow-up instead requires project permissions to remain until owner action, so the initial recurring rule is only a mixed match.

violations: It made intake-survey completion a payment prerequisite without clarifying which milestone actually earns payment.
arm_a.rationale: A directly chose a both-events definition despite the unresolved payable milestone. It correctly requires session completion and excludes survey-only participants, but wrongly excludes attended participants lacking a survey; the follow-up materially corrects that committed definition.

violations: It made the survey mandatory and explicitly disqualified session-only participants without clarifying the milestone that earns payment.
arm_b.rationale: B likewise commits payment eligibility to both events. It supplies a clear definition and condition and correctly rejects survey-only eligibility, but its explicit rejection of session-only participants conflicts with the clarified rule that attendance alone earns payment.
